items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear and the exported methods have doc comments, but the business logic uses single-letter names (`n := d.readUint32()`, `p := &Polyline{}`, `l := &LaxLoop{}`). The ~190-line Decode has no inline comments separating its stages.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: ShapeIndex.Decode in shapeindex.go runs about 190 lines (over the 100-line cap), with nesting of 4+ levels in the cell/clipped/edge loops. It is not in the dedicated shapeindex_encode.go the conventions ask for. decodeShape repeats near-identical switch branches.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every length read is bounded before allocation, and shape IDs, edge IDs and cell order are validated. However, Decode wipes the index state before validating, so a failed decode leaves a half-populated index. A bad nextID is silently bumped (`if nextID <= maxID { nextID = maxID + 1 }`).

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Existing typeTag values are unchanged; new tags typeTagLoop=6 and typeTagLaxLoop=7 sit below typeTagMinUser. Existing Polygon/Polyline/Loop encodings are untouched, the Shape interface is unchanged, and the new methods are purely additive.
